emotional-inertia.definition: how far a person's mood at one prompt predicts their mood at the next, measured as the lag-one correlation of their own mood series
emotional-inertia.excludes: average mood, how much mood varies, and any claim about what causes the carryover

esm.definition: a study design in which people answer short questions on a phone several times a day, so that mood is recorded close to the moment it is felt
esm.excludes: one-off questionnaires and recall of past weeks

lag-pair.definition: two adjacent prompts on the same study day, the earlier one called the lead; a missed prompt or a night breaks the pair
lag-pair.excludes: pairs that cross a night or skip a prompt

spike.definition: a lead prompt whose mood sits at least 1.5 of the person's own standard deviations from the person's own mean
spike.excludes: deviations judged against other people or against a population norm

recovery.definition: the median, over a person's spikes, of the share of each spike's distance from the person's mean that has gone by the next prompt, with 1 meaning back at the mean and 0 meaning no change
recovery.excludes: recovery measured in clock time, and recovery after events that did not produce a spike

ar1.definition: a series in which each value is the mean plus a fixed fraction of the previous value's distance from the mean, plus fresh random noise; the fraction is the single parameter
ar1.excludes: models with separate rates for small and large deviations, and models with measurement noise on top

pearson-r.definition: the correlation coefficient between two quantities measured on the same units, from -1 through 0 for no linear relation to 1
pearson-r.excludes: non-linear relations and any statement about cause

person-bootstrap.definition: an interval found by drawing people with replacement many times, recomputing the statistic each time, and taking the middle of the resulting spread
person-bootstrap.excludes: resampling of single prompts, which would treat one person's prompts as independent

split-half.definition: the correlation across people between a measure computed on one half of each person's data and the same measure on the other half; here the halves are odd and even study days
split-half.excludes: test-retest reliability over months, and the validity of the measure

factor-model.definition: a model that explains the correlations among several measured indicators by a smaller number of unseen common factors, fitted by maximum likelihood
factor-model.excludes: exploratory searches for the number of factors, and models of change over time

bic.definition: the Bayesian information criterion, a fit score that charges each extra parameter a penalty growing with sample size; the lower value is preferred
bic.excludes: a test of whether either model is true

kendall-bias.definition: the downward bias of a lag-one correlation estimated from a short series, about (1 + 3 phi)/n for a series of n values with true value phi (Kendall 1954)
kendall-bias.excludes: bias from measurement noise, which is a separate attenuation

attenuation.definition: the shrinking of an observed correlation toward zero when the measures that enter it are noisy
attenuation.excludes: a true weak relation between the underlying quantities

chi2-diff.definition: a test of whether a model with more free parameters fits nested data better than a simpler model, using the drop in the chi-square fit statistic against its degrees of freedom
chi2-diff.excludes: comparisons of models that are not nested
